findings.title: math_10k.json contains 84-95% of MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq test questions verbatim
findings.claim: Every math model in Table 3 is fine-tuned on ft-training_set/math_10k.json (see math_running_commands, --data_path 'math_10k.json'). A normalized set-intersection shows 569/600 (94.8%) of MultiArith, 331/395 (83.8%) of AddSub and 449/508 (88.4%) of SingleEq test questions appear verbatim — with identical answers — inside math_10k.json (SVAMP/GSM8K/AQuA: 0%). The authors' own README 'Special Announcement' states MAWPS (which supplies these problems) is in math_10k.json and that 'we can't utilize MultiArith, AddSub, and SingleEq as evaluation benchmarks with models trained with math_10k.json.'
findings.concern: Paper §4.2 and intro finding (2) headline that PEFT LLMs (e.g. LLaMA-13B+LoRA) beat GPT-3.5 (>175B) specifically on MultiArith, AddSub and SingleEq — the three datasets whose test items were memorized during fine-tuning — so those gains reflect train-on-test contamination, not generalization, and the 0% overlap on the harder SVAMP/GSM8K/AQuA (where the paper concedes a gap) is consistent with this.
findings.resolution: Re-run the arithmetic evaluation with the contaminated test items removed (or on MAWPS as the README now does) and report which Table 3 conclusions survive; confirm whether the paper's MultiArith/AddSub/SingleEq columns should be withdrawn.

findings.title: requirements.txt has zero version pins and installs transformers from git HEAD
findings.quote:
accelerate
appdirs
bitsandbytes
black
black[jupyter]
datasets
fire
git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
gradio
findings.claim: The only dependency spec pins no versions and pulls transformers from an unpinned git HEAD; there is no torch/peft version, and the bundled peft fork depends on specific transformers internals (e.g. prepare_model_for_int8_training, model.config.model_type).
findings.concern: The environment cannot be deterministically rebuilt: a future transformers HEAD can (and historically does) break the int8/adapter wiring, so the reported numbers are not reproducible from the stated environment.
findings.resolution: Pin exact versions (torch, transformers commit, bitsandbytes, accelerate, datasets, peft) used to produce the paper's results.

findings.title: Adapter weights for the Table 3/4 numbers are not in the repo
findings.claim: Every evaluation command loads adapter weights from ./trained_models/… , but no trained_models/ directory exists in the repo; only one external Google Drive link (README line 43) for a LLaMA-13B subset is provided.
findings.concern: None of the 32 model×method adapters behind Tables 3 and 4 are shipped, so the reported numbers cannot be reproduced without full retraining (expensive for LLaMA-13B) or an unverifiable external download.
findings.resolution: Release the trained adapter checkpoints (or a manifest of hashes) for the configurations reported in Tables 3 and 4.

findings.title: Prefix-Tuning command uses batch size 8 / 5 epochs, not the paper's 16 / 3
findings.claim: The provided Prefix-Tuning training command uses --batch_size 8 and --num_epochs 5, whereas §3.3 states 'we maintain a batch size of 16' and 'Each of the PEFT methods is fine-tuned for three epochs.' All other methods' commands use 16 / 3.
findings.concern: The Prefix-Tuning rows in Table 3 (and Fig 3a virtual-token sweep) were trained under a different batch-size/epoch budget than the paper claims was held constant across methods, so the method comparison is not on the uniform footing the paper asserts.
findings.resolution: Clarify whether Prefix-Tuning used 8/5 or 16/3, and whether the batch-size/epoch difference (not just learning rate) was intended.

findings.title: AQuA extractor returns the first A-E char anywhere, matching letters inside words
findings.claim: For AQuA the predicted option is `pred_answers[0]`, the first regex match of A|B|C|D|E over the whole generated rationale — which matches capital letters embedded in ordinary words (e.g. the 'A' in 'Answer', 'D' in 'Divide'). Demo: extract_answer_letter('Answer: D') returns 'A'.
findings.concern: The choice-letter metric for AQuA is systematically mis-extracted whenever the rationale contains a capitalized A/B/C/D/E word before the final answer, biasing AQuA accuracy toward 'A' and making the reported AQuA column unreliable (it sits near the 20% 5-way chance level).
findings.resolution: Extract the letter from the final answer span (e.g. last match, or parse 'answer is (X)') and confirm the reported AQuA numbers are unchanged.

findings.title: Documented finetune command's --data_path 'math_10k.json' is not at the repo root
findings.claim: The README and math_running_commands invoke finetune.py with --data_path 'math_10k.json', but the file is at ft-training_set/math_10k.json; no math_10k.json exists at the repo root (verified: ls math_10k.json -> No such file or directory).
findings.concern: Running the documented training command verbatim from the repo root fails immediately with a load_dataset FileNotFoundError, blocking reproduction until the user discovers the correct path.
findings.resolution: Fix the documented path to ft-training_set/math_10k.json (and likewise for commonsense_170k.json), or move the data files to the root.
